title: DamID
scope: Two-arm Illumina explanatory DamID schematic: in vivo adenine marking by a Dam–protein-of-interest fusion versus unfused Dam, followed separately by DpnI digestion, adapter ligation, DpnII digestion and selective PCR, then sequencing and comparison of mapped DNA. DamID-Seq names the sequencing readout implementation of DamID. The schematic is not a full library-construction recipe. Named Inducible DamID and NeuroDam variants in related abstracts are annotated for scope only; their unshown workflows are not merged into this graph. No origin date is assigned from the catalogue or publication dates.

operations.label: Create fusion protein / Split sample
operations.description: Establish separate cellular samples expressing either the fusion protein or unfused Dam. The fused Dam and protein-of-interest icon denotes the targeting construct. The drawing labels the two-arm arrangement “Split sample”; the primary implementation uses separate Dam-fusion and Dam-only genotypes. This record follows that implementation for arm provenance.
operations.mechanism: Low-level expression of a Dam–chromatin-protein fusion supplies the targeted catalyst; Dam alone supplies the control catalyst. Protein icons represent these catalysts, not substrates consumed by DNA digestion.
operations.information_effect: Sample provenance distinguishes targeted-plus-background methylation from the background control; no molecular barcode or pooling is depicted.

operations.label: DpnI digestion
operations.description: Cut methylated DNA from the fusion arm into fragments at Dam-marked sites; the DNA is changed from continuous molecules to a methylation-dependent restriction-fragment population.
operations.mechanism: DpnI selects adenine-methylated GATC-associated DNA by restriction cleavage.
operations.information_effect: Converts the DNA mark into fragment boundaries that can receive adapters; this chemical selection does not distinguish targeted from background methylation.

operations.label: Unmethylated GATCs are cut by DpnII

operations.label: PCR
